 4 more children die of measles-like symptoms as Health Ministry launches catch-up vaccination campaign Sm Najmus Sakib 16 November 2026 • Update : 16 November 2026 DHAKA, Bangladesh The death toll from dengue in Bangladesh rose to 502 after health authorities reported three more fatalities from the mosquito-borne disease.
 The total number of cases has crossed 164,000 since January, according to the Health Ministry.
 The death toll has risen from 336 last year, when nearly 85,000 cases were reported.
 Bangladesh usually experiences its dengue season between June and September.
 Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes. There is no specific treatment for the viral infection.
 4 children die of measles
 Separately, four more children died of measles-like symptoms, bringing the death toll from the infectious disease to 1,318 since mid-March this year.
 The Health Ministry registered 1,509 new cases of measles-like symptoms and 173 new confirmed infections nationwide.
 With the latest figures, the number of measles-like cases has crossed 249,500, while confirmed cases have exceeded 25,400.
 The Health Ministry has immunized more than 20.17 million children in response to the outbreak, in addition to routine vaccinations and a catch-up campaign launched late last month.
 Bangladesh historically had herd immunity against measles but has lost it in recent years due to declining vaccination coverage.
